steps.body: A **reflection** flips a shape across a line, like a mirror. Reflecting across the **x-axis** keeps x and flips the sign of y: (x, y) → (x, −y). Reflecting across the **y-axis** flips x: (x, y) → (−x, y).
Reflect the red triangle across the x-axis so it lands on the dashed target. A reflection flips every point to the opposite side of the mirror line — no sliding needed here.

widget.prompt: Flip the triangle across the x-axis onto the target.
widget.successFeedback: Reflected across the x-axis — every point's height flips to the opposite side, landing on the mirror image.
widget.offsetFeedback: The flip is right, but this one needs no sliding. Set dx and dy back to 0.
widget.reflectFeedback: Not a match yet — the target is the mirror image across the x-axis. Choose that reflection.

predict.prompt: The target is the triangle's mirror image below the x-axis. Can sliding alone — no flip — ever land it?

options.label: No — a slide can't turn a shape over
Only if the triangle were a square

predict.reveal: Slide the triangle down and its peak still points UP — the mirror image's peak points down. Translations keep orientation; reflections reverse it. No amount of sliding substitutes for the flip.

cml.actionGoal: Manipulate the model and track how it represents tm reflection.
invariants: The manipulated model and the mathematical relationship for tm reflection must stay consistent.
misconceptions: Changing a visible feature without preserving the relationship that defines tm reflection.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: What change would make the model stop representing the same mathematical relationship?

widget.prompt: Reflect the point (3, 5) across the x-axis. What is the image?

options.feedback: Right — across the x-axis, x stays and y flips sign: (3, −5).
That's a reflection across the Y-axis — across the X-axis, the Y flips: (3, −5).
Only the y flips across the x-axis; x stays 3: (3, −5).
Reflection doesn't swap coordinates — across the x-axis, y flips sign: (3, −5).

steps.body: The mirror line is what you flip ACROSS. Points keep their distance from the line but land on the opposite side. Across the x-axis, a point 5 above lands 5 below. The shape's size never changes.

explanationVariants: Across the y-axis, y stays and x flips sign: (2, 7) → (−2, 7).

widget.prompt: Reflect (2, 7) across the y-axis. What is the image?

commonEntries.feedback: That's a reflection across the X-axis — across the Y-axis, the X flips: (−2, 7).
Only x flips across the y-axis; y stays 7: (−2, 7).
Reflection doesn't swap coordinates — across the y-axis, x flips sign: (−2, 7).

widget.fallbackFeedback: Across the y-axis, y stays and only x flips sign.
widget.successFeedback: Right — across the y-axis, y stays and x flips sign: (−2, 7).

widget.prompt: The point (4, 1) became (4, −1). Which reflection was it?

panels.title: Conclusion
panels.body: Only y flipped, so it was a reflection across the x-axis (the horizontal mirror line).

widget.successFeedback: Exactly — when only y flips sign, the mirror line is the x-axis.

explanationVariants: (5, 2) → (−5, 2): only x flipped sign, so it was a reflection across the y-axis.
x flipped, y stayed — that's the y-axis mirror.

widget.prompt: A reflection sends (5, 2) to (−5, 2). Which line is the mirror?

options.label: The y-axis
options.feedback: Right — only x flipped sign, which the y-axis does.

options.label: The x-axis
options.feedback: The x-axis flips the Y-coordinate — here the X flipped, so it's the y-axis.

options.label: The line y = x
options.feedback: That line would swap the coordinates — here x just flipped sign, so it's the y-axis.

options.label: No line — it's a translation
options.feedback: The sign flip on x is a reflection, not a slide — the mirror is the y-axis.

explanationVariants: A reflection keeps size and shape identical — it only reverses the shape like a mirror image.
Reflections preserve size and shape; they just flip orientation.

widget.prompt: After a reflection, what is preserved?

options.label: The size and shape — it's a mirror image
options.feedback: Right — a reflection keeps the shape congruent, just flipped.

options.label: Nothing — the shape changes completely
options.feedback: A reflection keeps size and shape identical; only the orientation flips.

options.label: The size grows
options.feedback: Reflections never resize — the mirror image is exactly the same size.

options.label: The position but not the shape
options.feedback: It's the other way — the shape stays the same; it's the orientation that flips.

steps.body: Reflect across the x-axis, then read the result.
explanationVariants: Reflecting (−4, 6) across the x-axis keeps x and flips y: (−4, −6).
Across the x-axis: x stays −4, y flips to −6.

widget.prompt: Reflect (−4, 6) across the x-axis. What is the image?

commonEntries.feedback: Across the x-axis, the X stays the same (−4) and the Y flips: (−4, −6).
Only y flips across the x-axis; x stays −4: (−4, −6).
Reflection doesn't swap coordinates — across the x-axis, only y flips: (−4, −6).

widget.fallbackFeedback: Across the x-axis, x stays and only y flips sign.
widget.successFeedback: Right — x stays −4, y flips sign to −6.

hints: Across the x-axis, the x-coordinate stays and the y-coordinate flips sign.
So −4 stays −4. Now flip the y: 6 becomes −6.

steps.body: A reflection flips a shape across a mirror line, keeping size and shape.
takeaways: The mirror image is congruent — same size and shape, flipped orientation.

concept.body: A reflection flips a shape across a mirror line. Across the x-axis: (x,y)→(x,−y). Across the y-axis: (x,y)→(−x,y). Size and shape stay the same.

explanationVariants: Reflect (6, 3) across the x-axis: x stays, y flips, giving (6, −3).
Across the x-axis, only y flips sign: (6, −3).

widget.prompt: Reflect (6, 3) across the x-axis. What is the image?

options.feedback: Right — x stays 6, y flips to −3.
That's the Y-axis reflection — across the X-axis, the Y flips: (6, −3).
Only y flips across the x-axis; x stays 6: (6, −3).
Reflection doesn't swap coordinates — across the x-axis, y flips: (6, −3).
